statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement, so no current price path exists to score. Friday's inside-range close, a rotational session the index absorbed, and lower implied volatility keep Tail in the low band.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The single flagged window is the CME Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where a rejected Strait of Hormuz roadmap that Tehran has not yet received a formal answer on, a 10-year at a post-crisis high and a week of crude decline meet the thinnest liquidity of the week.
headline: Weekend halt keeps Tail at 6; rejected Hormuz roadmap and an inspection offer meet the 22:00Z reopen
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures have not traded since Friday 25 September settled at 21:00Z, so this assessment contains no live price-path evidence and says so explicitly. The newest verified tape is Friday's cash close: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 daily range and about 0.53% below the 30,770.63 52-week high, while the VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 against a 52-week range of 13.38 to 35.30. The S&P 500 closed at 7,743.41 (+0.51%), the Nasdaq Composite at 27,068.72 (+0.48%) and the Dow at 51,828.62 (+0.93%), which snapped a three-week losing streak.

Friday's internals remain the clearest evidence against a pathological path. Delayed latest-session context shows six of eight megacaps and six of seven semiconductors higher, with MSFT +3.66% and QCOM +3.97% against META -3.33% and INTC -3.45%, megacap dispersion 1.92 points and semiconductor dispersion 2.02 points, and Technology +0.85% against Communication Services -0.58%. A leading name retracing several percent while the index still closed higher is mean reversion working, not failing. That context is labelled non-real-time and cannot establish current NQ structure.

The macro backdrop is where Stress lives. The 10-year Treasury closed Friday at 5.18%, its highest since the financial crisis, with the 2-year at 4.87% on the 24 September H.15 release, and reporting through the week has focused on equities absorbing a bond sell-off rather than breaking on it. WTI was near 92.41 dollars, down about 2.33% on Friday and 7.4% on the week but still roughly 12.4% higher on the month, with Brent under 98 dollars; easing crude is what halted the yield surge into the close.

The weekend's live variable is diplomatic. Trump rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, a plan that asked for the naval blockade to be lifted, oil sanctions waived, roughly 12 billion dollars in frozen assets released and a ceasefire covering Lebanon and Yemen. Araghchi says Tehran has seen only an initial reaction and awaits Washington's definitive position through mediators. Offsetting that, Pezeshkian said Iran would readmit UN nuclear inspectors as part of negotiations, which keeps a track open. Saudi-led forces intercepted Houthi drones aimed at Riyadh and ballistic missiles toward Khamis Mushait on Saturday, an attritional pattern rather than a discontinuity.

Shared Finviz context collected at 01:54Z is fresh but partial: breadth, megacap, semiconductor and earnings sections are available while the futures and calendar sections failed, so cross-asset futures alignment could not be checked from that feed and the calendar was verified independently. No section of it is treated as live NQ price-path evidence.

Tail therefore stays at 6. There is no tape in which to observe shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, or an index holding near an extreme, and the last observed session was a two-way auction with declining implied volatility. Stress holds at 55 on a post-crisis high in long yields, an unresolved Gulf conflict, and a macro week carrying Core PCE on 30 September, ISM Manufacturing on 1 October and payrolls on 2 October, with Micron's fiscal fourth quarter after the close on 30 September as a semiconductor checkpoint. Confidence eases to 72 because the non-price evidence set is broad and freshly verified while the newest price evidence is roughly 29 hours old. The single flagged window is the Globex reopen from 22:00Z, where two days of unpriced headlines meet the thinnest liquidity of the week.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 02:00Z on Saturday 26 September to 01:00Z on Sunday 27 September, entirely inside the weekend halt that began at Friday's 21:00Z settlement. Every hour carries a published Claude assessment. Tail eased from 8 to 6 as Friday's inside-range close and declining implied volatility aged without contradiction, Stress rose from 45 to 54 on the rate and Gulf backdrop, and Confidence drifted from 84 down to 73 as price evidence aged. No hour in the window recorded persistent one-way structure or a failed retracement sequence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are almost entirely a closed market: CME Globex equity-index futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday 27 September, the twenty-first slot of this forecast. Conditional Tail therefore eases to 5 through the dead hours, drifts back toward 11 as the reopen approaches, and peaks at 15 in the reopen hour before easing to 13, 11 and 10 as live discovery resumes. Stress runs between 53 and 61 on a 10-year at a post-crisis high, an unresolved Hormuz standoff set against an Iranian offer to readmit nuclear inspectors, and crude about 7.4% lower on the week. Confidence troughs near 65 in the last closed hours before improving to 76 once roughly three hours of live tape exist. Every slot maps to EA_ON, and the only flagged window is 22:00Z to 23:59Z.
